claims.text: The starting material is a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
The starting material has a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
Stable intermetallic formation is associated with performance limitations in the Mg-containing alloy.
Thermal treatment can overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation.
The relevant alloy should have a density below 6 g/cm3.
Alloy composition is the structural mediator of the thermal-treatment effect.
Thermal treatment acts through relaxation of metastable phases.
Thermal treatment will improve room-temperature compressive behavior relative to the as-processed state.
Thermal treatment will improve corrosion resistance relative to the as-processed state.
Thermal treatment will improve resistance to high-temperature oxidation relative to the as-processed state.
The as-processed state is the experimental baseline.
A controlled thermal-treatment experiment will characterize resulting microstructure and properties.

contradictions.description: Thermal treatment is proposed as the intervention, but alloy composition is named as the mediator even though the treatment does not change bulk composition; no intervening composition-dependent microstructural variable is specified.
